alex: Quick handoff — short watchlist for overnight. TL;DR: noisy autoscale in eu-west, encoder tail latency drift on small batches, occasional 429s from dedupe-cache during bursts. Links and quick cmds below. :eyes:

maya: Thanks — can you paste the runbook links and exact alert IDs to silence if this is noise?

alex: Runbook: https://confluence.internal/redwood/oncall/watchlist — alert IDs: autoscale_kv_spike, encoder_tail_shift, dedupe_429_burst. Quick checks:
```
# check kv pods
kubectl get pods -l app=kv-engine -n prod -o wide
# tail recent autoscale logs
kubectl logs -l app=kv-engine -n prod --tail=200 | grep -i "scale up"
```

jonathan: FYI I flipped the eu-west autoscale policy to "noisy-threshold" for the night (will re-enable 08:00 UTC). Watching metrics. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Rotation update: alex handed off to maya (2368743210). Reminder: oncall shift ends 08:00 UTC.

maya: Got it. If encoder tail latency >250ms for >10m, we should rollback the canary. Who owns the canary now? @jonathan

jonathan: I'm owning it. I'll rollback if we cross thresholds. If dedupe 429s persist after 2 minutes, try a temporary cache capacity bump: `infra bump-cache --env prod --factor 1.5`. Ping infra oncall if you need help.

lee: Seeing a small prefetch KV miss-rate uptick on the grafana panel that lines up with the autoscale spikes. Not critical yet but correlated.

maya: Night checklist for me to follow: 1) mute autoscale_kv_spike if no backend errors, 2) monitor encoder tail panel, 3) confirm dedupe 429 cleared after bump, 4) call infra if bump fails. I'll leave a morning note. :coffee:

alex: One more note — avoid mass restarts; drain/evict one node at a time if you need to cycle. Reference logs: https://logs.internal/tx/abc123

maya: Acknowledged. oncall-bot, attach note: 'eu-west noisy autoscale & encoder tail watch' to the rotation page.

oncall-bot: Note recorded on rotation page: 'eu-west noisy autoscale & encoder tail watch' (2368743305).
